issues.description: Race condition on is_registered flag can cause concurrent requests to omit LoRA weights
issues.detail: In _create_trtllm_generate_request, the TritonLoraConfig.is_registered flag is set to True after building the request, but the actual inference is async. Two concurrent first-time requests for the same LoRA both see is_registered=False, but the second may set the flag and skip sending weights before the first request is actually executed by the backend, breaking inference. There is no lock and no confirmation the backend cached the LoRA.

issues.description: Mutating shared TritonLoraConfig from request path is not thread-safe
issues.detail: lora_config objects are shared singletons stored in model_metadata, but _create_trtllm_generate_request mutates lora_config.is_registered = True directly. Under concurrent requests this is a data race; combined with the registration logic above it can cause silent inference correctness bugs. Either guard with a lock or use a per-server registration registry with proper synchronization.

issues.description: _get_lora_config return type annotation lies about None possibility
issues.detail: The method is annotated as returning TritonLoraConfig, but it returns None when lora_name is None or lora_configs is None. Callers (chat/completion paths) pass the result into create-request helpers typed Optional. The annotation should be Optional[TritonLoraConfig] to avoid misleading type-checkers and reviewers.

issues.description: Possible NoneType crash when model_metadata.get(model_name) returns None
issues.detail: _get_lora_config calls self.model_metadata.get(model_name) and then immediately dereferences model_metadata.lora_configs without a None check. If the model name is not in metadata (e.g., a stale or invalid model_name passed through), this will raise AttributeError instead of a clean ClientError. Add a guard or raise a meaningful error.

issues.description: Variable shadowing of lora_config_path silently overrides the multi_lora.json path
issues.detail: Inside _parse_lora_configs, lora_config_path is first defined as the multi_lora.json path, then reassigned inside the loop to model.lora_config.npy for each entry. The outer name is no longer accessible after the first iteration; if future code references it after the loop it will get the wrong path. Rename the inner variable (e.g., lora_npy_config_path).

issues.description: Debug print statements left in production code paths
issues.detail: Multiple print(traceback.format_exc()) calls were added to fastapi routers (chat.py, completions.py, embeddings.py) and a print(f"backend: {backend}") inside _parse_lora_configs. These leak stack traces to stdout on every exception and add noisy per-request prints. Replace with proper logger.exception / logger.debug calls, or remove before merge.

review.summary: The PR extends LoRA support to TensorRT-LLM but introduces concurrency hazards around lazy LoRA registration: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered is mutated from request handlers without locking, and the flag is flipped before the backend has actually cached the weights, opening a race where concurrent first-use requests can skip sending lora_weights. Several smaller issues exist: variable shadowing of lora_config_path inside _parse_lora_configs, an Optional return value not reflected in the type annotation of _get_lora_config plus a missing None guard on model_metadata.get, and leftover debug prints/traceback dumps in routers. Tests now exercise both backends, which is good, but the registration concurrency semantics need to be fixed or documented before merge.
